A metal is heated with dil \(\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4\). The gas evolved is collected by the method shown in the figure. Answer the following questions based on it:

(The figure shows an upright gas jar standing in a trough of water, with a delivery tube entering near the bottom and gas bubbles rising up through the jar as the gas displaces the water.)

The gas is ______ than air and it is ______ in water.

Leave all the three test tubes for one day and then observe.

(The figure shows three test tubes, each containing an iron nail. Tube A: nail in water with ordinary air above it. Tube B: nail in boiled water with a layer of oil on top, sealing out air. Tube C: nail in dry air above anhydrous \(\text{CaCl}_2\), which absorbs all moisture.)

In which test tube is the nail rusted?

A metal is heated with dil \(\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4\). The gas evolved is collected by the method shown in the figure. Answer the following questions based on it:

(The figure shows an upright gas jar standing in a trough of water, with a delivery tube entering near the bottom; the gas bubbles rise up into the jar and displace the water downward and out.)

Name the method used for the collection of gas.

What is shown in the experiment given below:

(The figure shows a horizontal test tube clamped to a stand, containing a metal sample and glass-wool soaked in water. A burner heats the glass-wool to generate steam, which passes over the heated metal sample. The hydrogen gas produced travels through a delivery tube and is collected over water in an inverted jar labelled "Hydrogen".)

options.label: A
options.text: Reaction of metals with salt solutions

options.label: B
options.text: Heating a salt sample on a spatula

options.label: C
options.text: Action of steam on a metal

options.label: D
options.text: Testing the conductivity of a salt solution
